title: GLTF: Add import support for Draco and meshopt mesh compression

milestone.title: 4.x
milestone.description: Issues and pull requests slated for an undetermined Godot 4 release.

body:
This adds import support for compressed glTF files, covering `KHR_draco_mesh_compression`, `EXT_meshopt_compression`, and `KHR_mesh_quantization`. Files using these extensions were previously rejected with an error during import (#56613 added that rejection on purpose for Draco, since the extension was unsupported).

**Implementation**

Draco: decoding happens in `GLTFDocument::_parse_gltf_state()`, right after extension parsing. Each compressed primitive is decoded, and the attribute and index data is written back into the state as regular buffer views through `GLTFBufferView::write_new_buffer_view_into_state()`. The `KHR_draco_mesh_compression` entry is then removed from the primitive, so the rest of the import pipeline runs unchanged. When a compressed primitive has no `indices` accessor, one is synthesized from the decoded mesh. Decoded vertex data gets the 4-byte stride padding the spec requires for `ARRAY_BUFFER` buffer views.

meshopt: `EXT_meshopt_compression` buffer views are decoded into their fallback buffer right after buffer parsing, using the meshoptimizer decoder that already ships with the engine for LOD generation, then the extension entry is stripped. The ATTRIBUTES, TRIANGLES, and INDICES modes and the OCTAHEDRAL, QUATERNION, and EXPONENTIAL filters are covered. `KHR_mesh_quantization` is now listed as supported; the accessor decode path already implements the normalized-integer equations from the core specification, so default gltfpack output imports correctly.

Both decode paths validate everything against the glTF accessors before decoding, with a specific error message for each failure mode. Import only: the exporter never writes these extensions.

**Third-party**

Draco needs a vendored decoder: the decoder subset of Draco 1.5.7 (Apache 2.0) under `thirdparty/draco`, with encoders, command-line tools, tests, and the JS/WASM wrappers excluded. `thirdparty/README.md` and `COPYRIGHT.txt` are updated. meshopt needs no new third-party code. The Draco code is behind a `GLTF_HAS_DRACO` define and the meshopt code behind `MODULE_MESHOPTIMIZER_ENABLED`, so both can be excluded at build time.

**Binary size**

Measured on Windows x86_64 `template_release` (MSVC, same flags both sides): Draco adds 272 KB raw, the meshopt importer about 30 KB, 302 KB combined, or 0.44%. Zip-compressed the combined delta is 115 KB (0.43%). 2D-only templates are unaffected, since the glTF module is gated on `disable_3d`.

**Testing**

- Seven doctests in `modules/gltf/tests/`: GLB and separate `.gltf` imports for both codecs, default gltfpack output (meshopt plus quantization), and rejection of malformed data for each.
- Verified against the Khronos sample model Duck: the Draco variant and gltfpack output (quantized and unquantized) decode with geometry identical to the uncompressed original.
- The full test suite passes on Windows (1361 test cases, 419513 assertions).

Related to godotengine/godot-proposals#8576, which asks for Draco decompression hooks in GLTFDocument. This implements built-in support instead.

Draco support has been shipping in my Godot fork (Faster-Godot) since its 4.6.4 release; the meshopt and quantization support was written there as well.
